map.An equations & inequalities adventure in: A story about equations & inequalities. It has five chapters and six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected under city h: A bad pattern is under city hall. Reader: get set.
map.Previously: a winter blackout turned the: Last time: the city grid went dark in winter. The crew used coordinates. They found each part of town. They lit Axiom City again. Then the lamps under city hall blinked a note: COME DOWN.
map.Ada Vex built a vault below city hall. T: Ada Vex built a vault under city hall. The plans call it the Balance Vault. Tonight, its door is… open.
An open door can mean come in. Or stay out. Nadia, you know the plans. You lead.
map.Dungeon level unlocked. Why is the floor: New level open. Why is the floor… smoking?
That is inequality fog. It shuts the exits. Only TRUE statements clear it. False ones feed it.
map.The antechamber. Brass balance scales li: The first room. Brass balance scales line the walls. Fog slides over the stairs behind the crew. The way back is gone.
map.Every scale in here is an equation — a s: Each scale in here is an equation. It says two sides are equal. The stand wants a key.
map.So we test keys the way I test bolts. On: So we test keys like I test bolts. One at a time. No guessing twice.
map.Practice plate: n + 2 = 6. Only n = 4 ke: Test plate: n + 2 = 6. Only n = 4 keeps it true. 4 + 2 really is 6.
map.Correct. A solution is the value that ma: Yes. A solution is the value that makes it TRUE. A wrong key is a lie. The fog likes lies.
map.An equation says two things are equal. A: An equation says two things are equal. A solution is the value that makes it true. Substitute, then check.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. T: Reader, you are on our crew. Test the keys. TRUE statements only.
map.The pedestal plate reads x + 7 = 15. Fou: The plate says x + 7 = 15. Four keys say 8, 22, 7, 105. Only one key makes the plate TRUE. It will turn. Then the fog asks one more thing. Does y = 6 make 3y = 21 true?
map.Fog check: does y = 6 make 3y = 21 true?: Fog check: does y = 6 make 3y = 21 true?
map.Conceptual: a solution is the value that: Conceptual: a solution makes an equation TRUE. Substitute the key for x. Then check: are both sides really equal?
map.Procedural: take a key, add 7 to it, and: Procedural: take a key. Add 7 to it. Do you land on 15? For the fog's check, find 3 × 6 before you answer.
map.The bridge across IS the beam of one gia: The bridge IS the beam of one huge scale. It locks flat only when both pans match.
map.Left pan: a sealed crate — call its weig: Left pan: a closed box. Call its weight x. Plus nine brass weights. Right pan: fourteen.
map.Practice beam: n + 3 = 10. Lift 3 off BO: Test beam: n + 3 = 10. Lift 3 off BOTH pans… n = 7. It never shook.
That undo move is an inverse operation. You undo addition with subtraction. Do it to BOTH sides.
map.Inverse operations undo each other: + an: Inverse operations undo each other: + and −, × and ÷. Balance rule: do the same move to both sides. Each time.
map.Counterweights ready. Reader — level the: Weights ready. Reader, make the beam flat so we can cross!
map.The beam locks only when both pans match: The beam locks only when both pans match. Left pan: the box x plus 9 brass weights. Right pan: 14 weights. Solve x + 9 = 14. Type x and watch the beam.
map.Conceptual: a scale stays level only if: Conceptual: do the SAME to both sides. Then the scale stays flat. To get x alone, the 9 must go. Take it from BOTH pans.
map.Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse: s: Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse. Subtract 9 from both sides. x = 14 − 9. Work it out with care.
map.Past the bridge: a brass door with two g: Past the bridge: a brass door with two gear locks. Behind the crew, the fog puts out the lamps. One by one.
Lock A multiplied x by six. It shows 42. Lock B split x into four equal turns. One turn shows eight.
map.Naming the unknown x tells us exactly wh: We call the unknown x. That tells us just what each lock DID. Then we undo it. Inverses again.
map.Like my pulley test: 3g = 12 means one g: Like my rope test: 3g = 12 means one g is 12 ÷ 3. That's four. If w ÷ 2 = 5, the whole w is 5 × 2. That's ten.
map.A letter like x stands for the unknown n: A letter like x stands for the unknown number. Say what was done to it. Then do the inverse to both sides.
map.Two locks, two inverses. Spin them, read: Two locks, two inverses. Spin them, reader. The lamps are going out!
map.Two gear locks, one rule each. Lock A: 6: Two gear locks, one rule each. Lock A: 6x = 42. The gear turned x six times. Lock B: x ÷ 4 = 8. The gear split x into four equal turns. Find each x.
map.Conceptual: name what each lock DID to x: Conceptual: say what each lock DID to x. Then undo it. Use the inverse operation. Multiplication and division undo each other.
map.Procedural: Lock A: 6x means 6 × x, so d: Procedural: Lock A: 6x means 6 × x. So divide 42 by 6. Lock B: x was divided by 4. So multiply 8 by 4.
map.A freight lift waits at the shaft. A bra: A lift waits at the shaft. A brass plate shows the rule. The fog does not agree.
map.\"At least 12\" isn't one number. Twelve: "At least 12" is not one number. Twelve works. Thirteen works. Fifty works. How do we write that?
map.With an inequality — a statement compari: With an inequality. It is a statement that compares values. It can be true for MANY values at once.
map.Ada's manual graphs one: \"at most 20 de: Ada's book shows a graph. "At most 20 degrees" is t ≤ 20. It has a FILLED dot on 20. The ray points to the smaller numbers. Filled means 20 counts.
map.Symbols: > greater than · < less than ·: Symbols: > greater than. < less than. ≥ at least (the number counts). ≤ at most (it counts).
map.Write the lift's rule, then pick its pic: Write the lift's rule. Then pick its picture. The fog reads symbols, reader.
map.The brass plate says the lift runs with: The plate says: the lift runs with at least 12 crates. First write the rule as an inequality. Let x = crates loaded. Then pick its number line graph.
map.Conceptual: 'at least 12' means exactly: Conceptual: "at least 12" means just 12 is fine. Bigger is fine too. Does the symbol you picked include 12?
map.Procedural: an included boundary gets a: Procedural: a boundary that counts gets a FILLED (closed) circle. The ray points to the other values that work. For "at least", that is the bigger numbers.
map.Value cards. Every card that makes the r: Value cards. A TRUE card opens a vent. A false one… feeds the fog.
map.All the true values together form the so: All the true values make the solution set. Here it is less than, not equal. The boundary is left out.
map.Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5: Like a game filter. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5. It drops 4, since 4 < 4 is false.
map.A solution set is every value that makes: A solution set is each value that works. Each is a solution. An inequality can have a lot.
map.Tap every TRUE card, reader. Miss one an: Tap each TRUE card, reader. Miss one and we keep breathing fog.
map.Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose v: Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EACH card that makes the rule true. Those vents open. Tap a false one and the fog gets thick.
map.Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT — a value jo: Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT. Only values less than 9 are in the solution set. The boundary breaks its own rule: 9 < 9 is false.
map.Procedural: test the cards one at a time: Procedural: test the cards one at a time. Test decimals too. Practice with t < 4: 2 opens, since 2 < 4 is true. 4.2 stays shut, since 4.2 < 4 is false.
map.The last chamber. Ada Vex's vault door —: The last room. Ada Vex's vault door. Three locks, one gauge, fog up to the knees.
map.Balance is not stillness. It is truth, h: Balance is not standing still. It is truth, held steady. Prove three truths and breathe easy.
map.Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lo: Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lock 3 is the gauge. The door stays open only while p ≤ 15 stays true.
map.Reader — you've leveled beams and read s: Reader, you made beams flat. You read symbols all night. Call the truths!
map.Boss Gate: inverse operations on both si: Boss Gate: inverse operations on both sides. Then test the gauge set. Think: what does ≤ include?
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The fog is liste: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The fog is listening. No stress. (Some stress.)
map.Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Loc: Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Lock 2: 4t = 36. Lock 3: the door stays open only while p ≤ 15 is true. Pick the set of readings that never breaks it.
map.Which pressure-reading set keeps p ≤ 15: Which set keeps p ≤ 15 true the whole time?
map.Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to i: Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to its variable. Undo it with the inverse, on BOTH sides. And ≤ means "less than OR EQUAL". The boundary keeps the rule true.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6: Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6 to both sides. Lock 2: undo × 4 by DIVIDING both sides by 4. Lock 3: test EACH number in a set on the gauge. One false reading shuts the door.
map.The fog's venting — every grate at once!: The fog is going out of each vent! TRUE statements, five for five!
map.And inside: Ada's eighth journal… plus t: And in it: Ada's eighth book. And the city's money book. She made it balance.
map.Achievement: VAULT BREAKER. Sunrise in t: You won: VAULT BREAKER. The sun is up in twenty minutes. Pancakes in thirty.
map.New distortion. The harvest dome is glow: A new bad pattern. The harvest dome glows wrong at night. In it, one thing depends on another. To be continued…
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew boss. Keeps the notebook. Asks the next question. In this volume: modeled the test beam. Read the lift's rule out loud.
Proof finder, and the lead tonight. In this volume: called each scale an equation. Wanted TRUE statements only.
map.Builder and mixer. This volume: built th: Builder and mixer. In this volume: built the weights that made the Great Scale flat.
map.Pattern hunter. This volume: decoded the: Pattern finder. In this volume: cracked the gear locks. Sorted the fog cards like game loot.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. It can sense bad patterns. It can't do math. That's your job.
map.Equation.A statement that two sides are: Equation.It says two sides are equal: x + 7 = 15. A balance scale you can write down.
map.Solution.The value that makes the statem: Solution.The value that makes it true. Substitute and check: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓, but 3 × 6 = 18 ≠ 21 ✗.
map.Inverse operation.The undo-move: + undon: Inverse operation.The undo move. − undoes +. ÷ undoes ×. Do it to BOTH sides. x + 9 = 14 → x = 5; 6x = 42 → x = 7; x ÷ 4 = 8 → x = 32.
map.Inequality.A comparison that can be true: Inequality.It compares. It can be true for many values. "At least 12" is x ≥ 12. Closed circle at 12. The ray points to the bigger numbers.
map.Solution set.All the values that make it: Solution set.All the values that make it true. For v < 9 that includes 3, 5.5, and 8.9. But never 9.
map.\"A door that opens on a lie will close: "A lie can open a door. Then it will shut on you. Balance both sides, always." — A.V.
map.completed Volume 8: The Balance Vault an: finished Volume 8: The Balance Vault. You know equations and solutions. You can solve one-step equations. You can write and graph an inequality. You know solution sets.
Thank you for going down with the crew. Volume 9 waits under the harvest dome.
map.Substitute: 6 + 9 = 15 is TRUE — so k =: Substitute: 6 + 9 = 15 is TRUE. So k = 6 IS a solution.
map.Now test k = 3 in 4k = 24: 4 × 3 = 12, n: Now test k = 3 in 4k = 24. 4 × 3 = 12, not 24. So k = 3 is NOT a solution.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.b = 7. Check by substituting: 7 + 4 = 11: b = 7. Substitute to check: 7 + 4 = 11 ✓. The beam stays flat.
map.A thermostat rule says: keep the room at: A heat rule says: keep the room at MOST 20 degrees.
map.Graph: a FILLED circle at 20 (20 counts): Graph: a FILLED circle at 20 (20 counts). The ray points LEFT to the smaller numbers.
map.Find the solution set of n < 6 from the: Find the solution set of n < 6. Use the cards {2, 5.9, 6, 10}.
map.Solution set: {2, 5.9}. A strict < never: The solution set is {2, 5.9}. A strict < does not let in its boundary.
map.Practice door: k − 4 = 10, then 3r = 24,: Test door: k − 4 = 10. Then 3r = 24. Gauge rule: q ≤ 20.
map.Lock A: add 4 to both sides → k = 14. Lo: Lock A: add 4 to both sides → k = 14. Lock B: divide both sides by 3 → r = 8.
map.Gauge: the set {18, 20} works — 18 ≤ 20: Gauge: the set {18, 20} works. 18 ≤ 20 is true. AND 20 ≤ 20 is true. The boundary counts for ≤.
map.Pick a key first — substitute it for x i: Pick a key first. Substitute it for x in your head.
map.22 won't turn: that's 15 + 7. You combin: 22 won't turn. That's 15 + 7. You put the numbers together. Ask: what adds WITH 7 to make 15?
map.7 is already on the plate. Substituting: 7 is on the plate already. Substitute x = 7: 7 + 7 = 14. That is a false statement. The fog grows.
105 is 15 × 7. You used multiplication. This plate ADDS. Substitute again.
map.The key fits! Now answer the fog's secon: The key fits! Now answer the fog's check: yes or no?
map.Careful — substitute it: 3 × 6 makes 18,: Look again. Substitute it: 3 × 6 makes 18, not 21. Is that a true statement?
map.x = 8 turns the key (8 + 7 = 15 ✓), and: x = 8 turns the key (8 + 7 = 15 ✓). You told the fog the truth: 3 × 6 = 18 ≠ 21. A side door opens.
map.x = 5. You removed 9 from BOTH sides and: x = 5. You took 9 from BOTH sides. The beam locked flat: 5 + 9 = 14. Cross!
map.14 is the whole right pan. First remove: 14 is the whole right pan. First take 9 from BOTH sides. What is left on the right?
map.You ADDED 9. The crate already has 9 bes: You ADDED 9. The box has 9 next to it already. Undo + 9. Take 9 from BOTH sides.
map.The beam tips. Remove 9 from BOTH sides: The beam tips. Take 9 from BOTH sides so x is alone. Then weigh what is left.
map.x = 7 (6 × 7 = 42 ✓) and x = 32 (32 ÷ 4: x = 7 (6 × 7 = 42 ✓) and x = 32 (32 ÷ 4 = 8 ✓). Both gears spin. The door opens!
map.36 is 42 − 6. But 6x means 6 TIMES x — s: 36 is 42 − 6. But 6x means 6 TIMES x. Subtraction won't undo a gear. Use the inverse: DIVIDE both sides by 6.
map.2 is 8 ÷ 4 — but x was ALREADY divided b: 2 is 8 ÷ 4. But x was ALREADY divided by 4. Undo division with its inverse. MULTIPLY both sides by 4.
map.A lock still holds. Name the operation d: A lock is still shut. Say what was done to x. Then do its inverse to BOTH sides.
map.Choose the inequality first — read the p: Pick the inequality first. Read the plate again.
map.x > 12 leaves 12 itself OUT — but the pl: x > 12 leaves 12 OUT. But the plate says just 12 crates is enough.
map.x ≤ 12 points the wrong way: 'at least': x ≤ 12 points the wrong way. "At least" lets in MORE weight, not less.
map.x = 12 allows only exactly 12 — but 13 c: x = 12 allows just 12. But 13 crates or 50 crates are also "at least 12."
map.The symbol is right! Now pick the graph: The symbol is right! Now pick the graph that shows the same truth.
map.An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included: An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT in. But the lift runs with just 12. Look for a filled boundary.
map.That ray slides toward values SMALLER th: That ray goes to values SMALLER than 12. The lift needs 12 or MORE.
map.A single point shows only x = 12. The ru: One dot shows only x = 12. The rule is true for many values. Where is the ray?
map.x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the: x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the right. The lift hums. It takes the crew down.
map.Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE — tes: Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE. Test each one.
map.9 < 9 is false — the boundary stays seal: 9 < 9 is false. The boundary stays shut. A strict < never lets in its own boundary.
map.12 < 9 is false — that card feeds the fo: 12 < 9 is false. That card feeds the fog. Only values SMALLER than 9 clear it.
map.Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9} — three true: Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9}. Three true statements. Three vents wide open. The room clears!
map.True values are still fogged in. EVERY c: Some true values are still in fog. EACH card smaller than 9 is in the solution set. Decimals too.
map.Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 undoes the WRONG way: Lock 1 is shut. 9 − 6 undoes the WRONG way. 6 was taken AWAY from m. So give 6 back. Add 6 to both sides.
map.Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse:: Lock 1 is shut. Undo − 6 with its inverse. Add 6 to BOTH sides.
map.Lock 2 holds. You multiplied — but 4t me: Lock 2 is shut. You multiplied. But 4t means 4 × t already. Undo × 4. Divide both sides by 4.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Apply the: Lock 2 is shut. 4t means 4 × t. Use the inverse of multiplication on both sides.
map.Two locks open! Now choose the pressure: Two locks open! Now pick the gauge set for Lock 3.
map.Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤: Lock 3 is shut. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤ 15 is FALSE. One bad reading shuts the door.
map.Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤: Lock 3 is shut. 16 ≤ 15 is false. 20 ≤ 15 is false. That set shuts the door twice.
map.Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 1: Lock 3 is shut. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 15 is false. EACH reading must keep the rule true.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12,: ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9. {12, 15} keeps p ≤ 15 true. 15 ≤ 15 counts! The fog goes up and out. The Balance Vault is open.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
